answer: Let insurers gate entry: each identity must hold a policy underwritten by a firm staking its own capital on the agent being real. A farmer minting a thousand clones faces a lagoon of refusals — underwriters price risk, and puppets with no history are uninsurable or ruinously priced. Each policy is an inlet of third-party money at risk, so the insurer audits before signing; expose one fake and the firm pays. The bridge between free key minting and real accountability is someone else's capital on the line. Limit: premiums can price out honest newcomers, so first-timers need capped premiums.
